findings.scenario: CLEAN requires every GC row to cite governing SRC IDs in both current-evidence and gap/conflict cells. After reading GC-01, GC-04, GC-07, GC-08, GC-13, GC-22, GC-24, and GC-25, the gap/conflict cells have no SRC IDs (GC-04 and GC-22 use pronouns only). Later steps can treat those gaps as ungoverned or silently closed, so the matrix is not a source-bound contract.
findings.remediation: Put explicit SRC IDs in each listed gap/conflict cell, e.g. GC-01: SRC-03/SRC-20/SRC-23; GC-04: SRC-08–SRC-11; GC-07: SRC-15/SRC-20/SRC-22; GC-08: SRC-15/SRC-16; GC-13: SRC-04/SRC-22; GC-22: SRC-04/SRC-12/SRC-15; GC-24: SRC-12/SRC-14/SRC-15; GC-25: SRC-14/SRC-15/SRC-16.

findings.scenario: CLEAN requires exact normalized Deep Agents result paths. SRC-07 names the evaluation plan and `docs/eval/one-box-program/deepagents-js-spike-results-2026-08-29.md` but binds the companion receipt only as 'its adjacent `.json` receipt'. A differently named or missing JSON file can be treated as the T1–T11 disposition without a checkable path.
findings.remediation: Replace the adjacent-receipt phrase with the exact repository path of the normalized JSON receipt (or delete the claim if no such file exists).

findings.scenario: The six closed classes are not internally coherent. SRC-08 is a provisional routing policy classed as evaluation evidence, while GC-14 uses it as permission to retry. SRC-26 is a hash-bound closure receipt classed as evaluation evidence beside SRC-27/SRC-28 as audit evidence. Class-based ranking will treat policy as measured evidence and drop the foundation closure hash from the audit set.
findings.remediation: Reclass SRC-08 as proposed target (or accepted contract if that policy is in-force) and SRC-26 as audit evidence; keep GC uses aligned to the new classes.

findings.scenario: Band 1 names both the authority manifest and scoped implementation authorization, but the within-band paragraph ranks SRC-18, SRC-29, SRC-19, and SRC-01 only. SRC-02 is unclassified inside the band. If SRC-18 places operating-environment work in program scope while SRC-02 still sets implementationAuthorized capabilities to read/propose and prohibits provider/network/persistence, a reader can take the manifest as the winning machine-readable owner.
findings.remediation: Add one within-band-1 rule: SRC-02 exclusively owns implementationAuthorized, allowed effects, and prohibitedCapabilities and cannot be overridden by SRC-18, SRC-19, SRC-29, or SRC-01.

findings.scenario: GC-07 current evidence cites only SRC-20/SRC-22 and the gap says no immutable segment, mid-turn, stale-result, or receipt-link rule is specified. SRC-15 TM-05 already requires a new receipted route segment on every user-requested switch and forbids hidden fallback. Steps 2–3 can treat route segments as greenfield and under-bind the threat model.
findings.remediation: Move SRC-15 into GC-07 current evidence; restate the gap as missing schema/state-machine/receipt fields under that already-governing rule.

audit.proof_assessment: The supplied handoff, OBX-AUTH-ATF-001, ADR 0003, routing policy, and frozen-foundation receipts show the provider-offline, no-authorization, Canvas, Page-IR, and route-preservation decisions were not reversed. The new matrix bytes themselves are the deterministic proof that CLEAN citation, exact Deep Agents path, class-coherence, and within-band-ranking bars are unmet; prior Grok items in those areas are only partly dispositioned.
residual_risks: GC-12 is owned by Step 4 in P180-R009 but marked open-to-step-5, so capacity ceilings may be deferred past the budget contract.
SRC-03 `:15-31` may not point at the roster paragraph, weakening the persistent-identity freeze.
Without the exact JSON path, GC-06 can keep citing T1–T11 after the receipt is renamed or split.
